description: The Self-Healing settings page in the qontinui-runner desktop application, accessed via the 'Self-Healing' tab in the Settings sidebar. It configures three automation self-healing subsystems: Action Caching (TTL-based cache that avoids redundant template matching and screen captures), Visual Validation (post-action screen state verification to detect failed actions), and LLM Assistance (AI-powered element recovery using local Ollama or remote OpenAI/Anthropic APIs). Each subsystem is presented as an independently collapsible section with a toggle switch or mode selector. When LLM Mode is set to Remote API, the page adds API key management backed by the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager) — separate from the main settings file. All six settings fields are persisted via the save_self_healing_settings Tauri IPC command and passed directly to the qontinui Python library at workflow execution time. The SelfHealingSettings Rust struct is the canonical type; the TypeScript interface mirrors it exactly.

groups.name: Page Structure
groups.description: The self-healing tab renders a titled page header, a descriptive subtitle, and three collapsible section panels. This group verifies the top-level structure is present after settings have loaded.

assertions.description: The heading 'Self-Healing Configuration' is displayed at the top of the self-healing tab
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded (loading indicator is gone)

assertions.description: The description text beginning with 'Configure automation self-healing features including action caching, visual validation, and LLM-assisted recovery' is visible below the heading
The 'Action Caching' section header is present on the page
The 'Visual Validation' section header is present on the page
The 'LLM Assistance' section header is present on the page

groups.name: Loading State
groups.description: When the page first mounts, it fetches settings via the get_self_healing_settings Tauri IPC command. During this fetch, a loading indicator is shown in place of the settings form. This group verifies the loading and transition-to-loaded behavior.

assertions.description: While settings are being fetched, an element with data-content-label 'loading self-healing settings' is present and displays the text 'Loading self-healing settings...'
assertions.precondition: Page has just mounted and the get_self_healing_settings fetch has not yet completed

assertions.description: After settings are loaded from the backend, the loading indicator disappears and is replaced by the three collapsible section headers (Action Caching, Visual Validation, LLM Assistance) and the Save / Reset buttons

groups.name: Action Caching Section
groups.description: A collapsible panel with a section header containing a toggle switch. Clicking the header expands/collapses the body. When expanded, it shows a Cache TTL number input (min 30, max 3600, step 30 seconds) and an info box explaining the caching behavior. The TTL input is disabled when the toggle is off. Defaults: enabled=true, ttl=300.

assertions.description: The Action Caching section header shows the subtitle text 'Cache action results to avoid redundant operations'

criteria.textContent: Cache action results to avoid redundant operations

assertions.description: When the Action Caching section is expanded, a label 'Cache TTL (seconds)' is visible above the number input

When expanded, the Action Caching section shows an info box with text 'Action caching prevents redundant template matching and screen captures when the same action is performed repeatedly within the TTL window.'

criteria.textContent: Action caching prevents redundant template matching

assertions.description: Clicking the Action Caching section header toggles the body. When collapsed, the TTL input and info box are hidden. When expanded, they appear. The chevron icon faces down when expanded and right when collapsed.

When the Action Caching toggle switch is turned off, the Cache TTL number input becomes disabled and non-interactive. Turning the toggle back on re-enables the input. This prevents editing a TTL that will be ignored.

groups.name: Visual Validation Section
groups.description: A collapsible panel with a toggle switch in the header. When expanded, it shows only an info box explaining that actions are validated by checking expected screen state after execution. There are no additional configuration fields. Defaults to enabled=true.

assertions.description: The Visual Validation section header shows the subtitle 'Validate actions by checking screen state after execution'

criteria.textContent: Validate actions by checking screen state after execution

assertions.description: When the Visual Validation section is expanded, an info box displays: 'When enabled, actions are validated by checking if the expected screen state is achieved after execution. This helps detect and recover from failed actions.'

criteria.textContent: When enabled, actions are validated by checking

assertions.description: The Visual Validation section has a toggle switch in its header row. Toggling it off sets visual_validation_enabled=false. This disables post-action screen state checking in the qontinui Python library for subsequent workflow runs.

groups.name: LLM Assistance Section — Mode Selector
groups.description: A collapsible panel without a toggle switch (unlike the other two sections). It contains an LLM Mode dropdown with three options. The selected mode determines which sub-configuration panel appears below the dropdown. An info box is always shown at the bottom of the expanded section. Defaults to mode=disabled.

assertions.description: The LLM Assistance section header shows the subtitle 'Use AI to assist with element identification and recovery'

criteria.textContent: Use AI to assist with element identification and recovery

assertions.description: When expanded, a label 'LLM Mode' is visible above the mode dropdown

The LLM Mode dropdown has exactly three options: 'Disabled' (with description 'No LLM assistance for self-healing'), 'Local Ollama' (with description 'Use locally running Ollama instance'), and 'Remote API' (with description 'Use cloud API (OpenAI/Anthropic)'). The selected option's description is displayed below the dropdown.

Changing the LLM Mode dropdown value conditionally shows/hides sub-configurations: selecting 'Local Ollama' reveals the Local Ollama Configuration sub-section and hides Remote API; selecting 'Remote API' reveals Remote API Configuration and hides Local Ollama; selecting 'Disabled' hides both sub-sections.

The LLM Assistance section contains an info box with text: 'LLM assistance enables AI-powered element identification when template matching fails, helping to recover from dynamic UI changes and improve automation reliability.'

criteria.textContent: LLM assistance enables AI-powered element identification

groups.name: LLM Assistance — Local Ollama Configuration
groups.description: When LLM Mode is 'Local Ollama', a sub-section appears labeled 'Local Ollama Configuration' with a Server icon. It contains a single Model Name text input defaulting to 'llava'. This model name is passed to the qontinui Python library to address a locally running Ollama instance for visual understanding tasks during automation recovery.

assertions.description: The element with data-content-label 'ollama config heading' showing 'Local Ollama Configuration' is visible when LLM Mode is Local Ollama
assertions.precondition: LLM Assistance is expanded and LLM Mode is set to Local Ollama

assertions.description: A text input labeled 'Model Name' is visible with placeholder text 'llava' and help text 'Model to use for visual understanding (e.g., llava, bakllava, llava-phi3)'
assertions.precondition: LLM Assistance is expanded and LLM Mode is Local Ollama

assertions.description: The Local Ollama Configuration sub-section is hidden when LLM Mode is 'Disabled' or 'Remote API'. It renders only when LLM Mode is exactly 'local_ollama'. Switching away from Local Ollama immediately removes the model name input from the DOM.

groups.name: LLM Assistance — Remote API Configuration
groups.description: When LLM Mode is 'Remote API', a sub-section appears labeled 'Remote API Configuration' with a Cloud icon. It contains an API Provider dropdown (OpenAI or Anthropic) and an API key management area. Changing the provider triggers a fresh keychain check. This sub-section is exclusive to Remote API mode.

assertions.description: The element with data-content-label 'remote api config heading' showing 'Remote API Configuration' is visible when LLM Mode is Remote API
assertions.precondition: LLM Assistance is expanded and LLM Mode is set to Remote API

assertions.description: A label 'API Provider' is visible above the provider dropdown with two options: 'OpenAI' (value 'open_ai') and 'Anthropic' (value 'anthropic')
assertions.precondition: LLM Assistance is expanded and LLM Mode is Remote API

assertions.description: Switching the API Provider dropdown between OpenAI and Anthropic immediately triggers the has_self_healing_api_key Tauri command for the newly selected provider. The API key management area updates to reflect whether a key exists for that provider — without requiring a page reload or save action.
The Remote API Configuration sub-section is hidden when LLM Mode is 'Disabled' or 'Local Ollama'. It renders only when LLM Mode is exactly 'remote_api'.

groups.name: API Key Management — Two-State UI
groups.description: The API key area within Remote API mode has two mutually exclusive states. State A (no key): shows a password input with Show/Hide toggle and a 'Save API Key' button (disabled until input is non-empty). State B (key exists): shows a muted 'API key configured' status element and a red 'Remove' button. Transitions between states happen immediately on save or remove. The key is stored in the OS keychain, not the settings file.

assertions.description: When an API key is stored in the keychain for the selected provider, the element with data-content-label 'api key configured' is visible and a 'Remove' button is present in the API key area
assertions.precondition: LLM Mode is Remote API and the selected provider has an API key in the OS keychain

assertions.description: A 'Save API Key' button is present when no key is configured. It is disabled when the API key input is empty and enabled when at least one character has been entered.
assertions.precondition: LLM Mode is Remote API and no API key is configured for the selected provider

assertions.description: Entering a non-empty value in the API key input and clicking 'Save API Key' calls save_self_healing_api_key with the selected provider and entered key. On success, the input disappears and the 'API key configured' status element becomes visible. The input is cleared and the Show/Hide toggle is hidden.
assertions.precondition: LLM Mode is Remote API, no key configured, and a non-empty key has been typed in the input

assertions.description: Clicking 'Remove' (when key is configured) calls delete_self_healing_api_key for the selected provider. On success, the 'API key configured' status disappears and the password input returns, allowing a new key to be entered.
assertions.precondition: LLM Mode is Remote API and API key is configured for the selected provider

assertions.description: The API key is stored exclusively in the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager) via the Tauri backend — not in the settings JSON file. The help text 'API key is stored securely in the OS keychain' confirms this. A consequence is that the six main settings fields (action_caching_enabled, cache_ttl_seconds, etc.) and the API key are saved independently via separate Tauri commands and separate button presses.

criteria.textContent: API key is stored securely in the OS keychain

assertions.precondition: LLM Mode is Remote API and no key is currently configured

groups.name: Action Buttons — Save and Reset
groups.description: Two action buttons appear at the bottom of the page. 'Reset to Defaults' (left, muted) restores all form fields to their default values in-memory without saving. 'Save Self-Healing Settings' (right, primary) calls save_self_healing_settings and shows animated state feedback during and after the save.

assertions.description: A 'Save Self-Healing Settings' button is present at the bottom right of the page
A 'Reset to Defaults' button is present at the bottom left of the page

Clicking 'Save Self-Healing Settings' triggers three sequential button states: (1) default: Heart icon + 'Save Self-Healing Settings', (2) in-flight: spinner icon + 'Saving...' and the button is disabled, (3) success: check icon + 'Saved!'. The button is re-enabled and returns to the default state after the save completes.

Clicking 'Reset to Defaults' immediately restores all form fields in-memory to: action_caching_enabled=true, cache_ttl_seconds=300, visual_validation_enabled=true, llm_mode='disabled', ollama_model='llava', api_provider='open_ai'. The page updates visually without a round-trip to the backend. A subsequent Save is required to persist these defaults.
assertions.precondition: Settings have been modified from their defaults

groups.name: Feedback Alerts — Error and Success
groups.description: The page shows contextual alerts at the top of the form area (above the sections) in response to save operations. Success alerts auto-dismiss after 3 seconds. Error alerts persist until the next user action clears them.

assertions.description: After a successful save operation, a green success alert appears with the text 'Settings saved successfully!' and automatically disappears after approximately 3 seconds
assertions.precondition: A save operation has just completed successfully

assertions.description: If the save_self_healing_settings Tauri command returns success=false or throws an error, a red error alert appears at the top of the form displaying the backend's error message string. The alert persists until the next action or page navigation.

target.label: Settings page heading (error alert appears above it)

assertions.precondition: A save operation has returned an error from the Tauri backend

groups.name: Settings Persistence and Data Model
groups.description: Self-healing settings are persisted via save_self_healing_settings and retrieved via get_self_healing_settings. The data model has exactly six fields. API keys are stored separately in the OS keychain. This group verifies the round-trip integrity and the semantic contract of the settings object.

assertions.description: After saving modified settings (e.g., action_caching_enabled=false, cache_ttl_seconds=600, llm_mode='local_ollama', ollama_model='bakllava'), navigating to a different Settings tab and returning to 'Self-Healing' should show all saved values still applied in the form — no reversion to defaults
assertions.precondition: Settings have been saved and the user navigated away and back

assertions.description: The settings object passed to save_self_healing_settings contains exactly these six fields: action_caching_enabled (boolean), cache_ttl_seconds (integer, 30-3600), visual_validation_enabled (boolean), llm_mode (one of 'disabled', 'local_ollama', 'remote_api'), ollama_model (string), api_provider (one of 'open_ai', 'anthropic'). The API key is excluded — it travels via a separate keychain command. Any validation error from the Rust backend (e.g., invalid llm_mode string) surfaces as a red error alert.

The self-healing settings are passed directly to the qontinui Python library when executing workflows. The description text 'These settings are passed to qontinui Python when executing workflows' confirms this contract. Changes saved here take effect on the next workflow run without requiring a runner restart. The six fields map 1:1 to the SelfHealingSettings Rust struct serialized into the Python subprocess invocation.

criteria.textContent: passed to qontinui Python when executing workflows
